purpose: Freeze an independently selected multisite exact-day nuclear/special-weapons aerial-event cohort inside the POSS-I study window before any Palomar observation-day membership lookup for the new holdout dates.

cohort_roles.HOLDOUT_PRIMARY_NEW: Date was selected from independently sourced Earth records and its Palomar observation-day membership has not been consulted for R4 selection.
cohort_roles.CALIBRATION_REUSE_KNOWN_OUTCOME: Previously tested date retained only for calibration/context; excluded from the R4 primary significance statistic because its Palomar outcome is already known.
cohort_roles.PROVISIONAL_NOT_PRIMARY: Historically relevant candidate that is not primary-test eligible until its source/date binding meets the frozen evidence rule.

source_selection_firewall.source_requirement: Exact calendar day plus federal/official archival release lineage or stronger. Primary file URL/identifier and source limitations remain explicit.

The OSI summary table records a Sandia Base observation on 22 March 1950 described as a round blue-centered/orange-exterior object crossing part of the sky before burning out. R4 records only that the official table contains an exact-day aerial observation; it does not promote interpretation.

rows.reported_summary: An FBI record states that at about 22:45 on 10 May 1952 four DuPont employees at the Savannah River Plant saw four disk-shaped objects approaching the 400 Area, followed by additional reported objects at approximately 23:05, 23:10 and 23:25. R4 collapses all reports to one site-date.

An FBI Savannah urgent teletype records that the AEC Security Office reported two DuPont employees saw a blue light with an orange fringe shaped like a saucer over the Savannah River Plant 400 Area at approximately 21:30 on 8 August 1952.
